prop:cs-evaluation-faithfulness:
Proposition Faithfulness of the Chern--Simons evaluation on the brane tower. Let \Phi_n(K) denote the tower-level volume contribution from the tower decomposition. Let \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) denote the n-th quantum characteristic class.

The Chern--Simons evaluation map is faithful at each tower level. For every hyperbolic knot or link K in the Descartes spectrum,

  \kappa_n \neq 0 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \Phi_n(K) \neq 0.

If \kappa_n defines a non-trivial obstruction in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}), the Chern--Simons period integral over the n-th twisted sector yields a non-zero real contribution to \mathrm{Vol}(K).
rem:cs-evaluation-faithfulness-corollari:
Remark Corollaries of Chern--Simons faithfulness and relation to Mostow rigidity. Corollaries.

  1. No accidental cancellation. The Peiffer identity in the crossed groupoid conjugates a^{(n)} by g^{(n)} but preserves the period. The \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)-adjoint action functions as an automorphism of the band \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}, not as a projection to zero.
  2. Infinite non-trivial contributions. The Yekutieli lifting theorem guarantees \kappa_n \neq 0 for all n. Faithfulness therefore implies the volume receives new data at every tower level.
  3. Path to algebraic independence. If each \Phi_n(K) carries arithmetically independent data, the series \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = \sum_n \Phi_n(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) = \sum_n \Phi_n(5_2), and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = \sum_n \Phi_n(\mathcal{B}_3) satisfy no polynomial relation. A finite polynomial cannot absorb infinitely many independent contributions.

Relation to Mostow rigidity. Mostow rigidity guarantees the total volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) defines a topological invariant. This proposition refines the invariant into a graded series \{\Phi_n(K)\}_{n \geq 0}, controlled by cohomological obstructions. Rigidity ensures convergence. Faithfulness ensures non-degeneracy at each grade.
conj:single-volume-irrationality:
Conjecture Irrationality of a single hyperbolic knot volume. Each of the three non-zero QOU hyperbolic volumes is irrational:

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) \notin \mathbb{Q},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \notin \mathbb{Q},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \notin \mathbb{Q}.

Remark. This conjecture remains open. No hyperbolic 3-manifold volume has ever been proven irrational. The figure-eight volume 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) evaluates the Clausen function at a rational multiple of \pi. Its irrationality reduces to the irrationality of \mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \sin(k\pi/3)/k^2. This represents a Dirichlet L-value at s = 2 for the character \chi_{-3}. This evaluation remains unknown.

Ap'ery (1978) proved \zeta(3) \notin \mathbb{Q}. The constant \zeta(3) equals one-quarter the hyperbolic volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. Knot complement volumes sum Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm values D(z_i) at algebraic arguments. The arithmetic of these sums lies beyond current methods.

Irrationality forms the weakest link in the transcendence chain:

  \text{irrationality}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \mathbb{Q}\text{-linear independence (Borel--Zagier)}
  \;\Longleftarrow\;
  \text{algebraic independence.}

Proving any of these statements for the QOU volumes demands a breakthrough in transcendental number theory.
conj:borel-zagier-qou-volumes:

  a_1 \,\mathrm{Vol}(4_1) + a_2 \,\mathrm{Vol}(5_2)
  + a_3 \,\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 0,
  \quad a_i \in \mathbb{Q}
  \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\;
  a_1 = a_2 = a_3 = 0.

This represents a special case of the Borel--Zagier conjecture. The Borel--Zagier conjecture asserts the \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of volumes of pairwise non-commensurable hyperbolic 3-manifolds.
conj:three-knot-jet-order-independence:
Conjecture Jet-order algebraic independence (QOU-attackable reduction). For every truncation order N, the Habiro-ring expansions of the coloured-Jones invariants for the three QOU knots/links,

  J_{4_1}(q),\qquad J_{5_2}(q),\qquad J_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q)
  \;\in\; \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]},

are algebraically independent modulo (q;q)_{N+1} over \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}]. Equivalently, the Jacobian of their cyclotomic coefficient vectors \bigl(c_0(K), \dots, c_N(K)\bigr) for K \in \{4_1, 5_2, \mathcal{B}_3\} possesses full rank 3 for all N \ge N_0.

This statement supplies a computationally viable target. It implies the algebraic-independence conjecture provided the surreal-limit bridge holds. The ideal approach requires the full transcendence machinery (Grothendieck periods and the Borel regulator on K_3(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})), which remains out of reach. This reduction replaces that machinery with three framework-native tools and one remaining gap.

Finiteness and decidability. Each J_K(q) admits a canonical jet-order grading. The Habiro cyclotomic expansion J_K(q) = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n(K)\,(q;q)_n organizes the invariant such that the n-th term forms the vertical jet-degree n component of the categorical generating function. This aligns with the body-order filtration grading the binding series G(x;q) = \sum_n B_n x^n. Algebraic independence to order N imposes a finite-rank condition on the truncated coefficient matrix. The claim is strictly decidable.

The three framework tools.

  1. Jet-order filtration supplies the grading. Independence is verified order-by-order. Reid (1991) anchors the base order. Because 4_1 is the unique arithmetic hyperbolic knot, its trace field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) is rigidly distinct from the cubic trace field of 5_2 and the link field of \mathcal{B}_3 at order 0.
  2. Gröbner–Shirshov filtration certifies each order. The reduction engine computes the elimination ideal I_N = \bigl(\text{relations among } J_{4_1}, J_{5_2}, J_{\mathcal{B}_3} \bmod (q;q)_{N+1}\bigr) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}[q,q^{-1}][x,y,z]. Full Jacobian rank holds if and only if I_N carries no generator of total degree \le N. This translates "no polynomial relation" into a normal-form computation natively executed by the skein engine. The base-order certificate is proved and directly witnessed by computation. The h-jet expansion about q=1 of the canonical Markov traces \mathrm{tr}_M(K) for the three canonical braid words yields jet-Jacobian rows (\tfrac14, -1, \tfrac{55}{16}), (\tfrac12, 0, -\tfrac1{16}), and (1, 0, 0). Their elimination determinant is \tfrac1{16} \neq 0 (LU pivots (\tfrac14, 2, \tfrac18)). Full rank 3 holds unconditionally at the base order. This constitutes a finite determinant test on real data. Higher orders require no further computation. The order-N Jacobian contains this non-singular 3\times3 minor as a column-submatrix. Its rank is therefore \ge 3. The three rows strictly bound the rank by 3. The rank must be exactly 3 at every N, as rank is monotonically non-decreasing in the column count. The two endpoints of this argument are proved. The base minor is full-rank via explicit invertibility. The abstract monotonicity principle holds: any monotone, row-bounded rank function equal to 3 at the base order remains 3 for all N \ge 3. The column-extension linkage discharging the principle's hypotheses for the order-N Jacobian is supplied as a structural input. Per-order independence reduces to this structural linkage.
  3. Surreal error bounds supply the bridge to the limit. The correct geometric picture is parallel transport on the projective state fibre. The coloured-Jones invariant J_K(q) acts as the holonomy of the categorical connection, parallel-transported along the substrate q-deformation path on \mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{CP}^1. The volume is its singular-limit asymptotics \mathrm{Vol}(K) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{2\pi}{n}\log\lvert J_K(e^{2\pi i/n})\rvert. The surreal error bound measures the transport error as q deforms toward the root-of-unity point. This error is non-Archimedean because the target point is a singularity of the connection. The error is an infinitesimal in the surreal field. Three conditions must hold for the bridge:
    • (I1) Uniformity in jet order. The transport error must be bounded uniformly in N. The connection's curvature is uniformly controlled along the deformation path, independent of the truncation order. Any error growing with N severs the transfer.
    • (I2) Archimedean projection. The error inhabits the surreal fibre level, carrying the \mathrm{Im}(q) structure. The volume is archimedean (\mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0). The surreal infinitesimal must project to exactly 0 under \tau. A non-infinitesimal archimedean shadow would inject a spurious polynomial relation among the volumes.
    • (I3) Monodromy separation. Transport around the cusp is flat only at generic q. At the root-of-unity limit, the holonomy accumulates cusp/modular monodromy. The bound must isolate the physical holonomy, which yields \mathrm{Vol}, from this monodromy artifact. The framework's surreal-number error field provides the natural setting for this uniform bound. The reduction splits the previously monolithic hypothesis. Uniformity (I1) and the (I2)∘(I3) composition are proved. The two physical inputs remain conjectural: the physical-holonomy shadow vanishes (I2), and the monodromy shadow vanishes (I3). These are now isolated as precisely stated hypotheses.

The one remaining gap. This reduction does not prove the deep conjecture. It reduces the conjecture to a single native lemma:

Bridge lemma (open). If \{J_{4_1}, J_{5_2}, J_{\mathcal{B}_3}\} are jet-order independent for all N with a surreal-bounded uniform error, then \{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\} are algebraically independent over \mathbb{Q}(q_0).

The reduction secures a strategic advantage. It shifts the algebraic-independence conjecture from an intractable Grothendieck-period transcendence statement to a finite, per-order computation coupled with the surreal bridge. The base order is now certified. The (I1) uniformity and composition properties of the bridge are proved. Unconditional closure is sacrificed: the (I2) and (I3) physical inputs remain unproved. This converts an external dead end into an internal, incremental research target structured natively on the framework's filtration.

This section examines the Yekutieli transcendence shadow and the physical consequences of algebraic independence versus dependence among knot volumes, proves that the alternating-channel product formula generates the baryon period from the three-strand representation, records the golden-ratio degeneration of the Descartes elliptic curve at q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2, and establishes the golden-skew dual node identity over \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5}).
rem:formal-chain-transcendence:
Remark The formal derivation chain does not depend on transcendence status. The formal proof chain operates in the Laurent polynomial ground ring \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. It does not use real-number arithmetic. Hyperbolic volumes enter only through the specialisation \iota \colon q \mapsto q_0. They appear as computed invariants verified to 10^{-14} precision via SnapPy.

The topological mass formula \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^2 mixes Laurent polynomials in q with hyperbolic volumes. The categorical derivation uses the Hecke algebra, Skein relations, Gröbner--Shirshov normal forms, and transfer matrices. This derivation remains purely algebraic over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. It does not depend on whether \mathrm{Vol}(K) is transcendental, algebraic, or irrational.

The algebraic independence conjecture describes the number-theoretic structure of the physical coefficient ring. No result requires this conjecture. If a polynomial relation holds among the volumes, the mass predictions and categorical structure remain valid. Only the algebraic structure of the coefficient ring simplifies. The conjecture asserts exactly that the specialisation map \iota is injective on the extended ring \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)].
rem:yekutieli-transcendence-shadow:
Remark Algebraic independence as the transcendence shadow of non-vanishing obstructions. The quantum characteristic classes \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) obstruct lifting at every level of the cosimplicial crossed groupoid. The classes \kappa_n vanish exactly at the levels n \mid \chi(A) and persist at every other level (item 3 of the QU-to-QOU theorem). Since infinitely many levels survive, the brane tower never collapses to finite height (Yekutieli lifting).

Each hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the classical limit (q \to 1) of the quantum dilogarithm sum across the brane tower. A polynomial relation P(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) = 0 over \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}] would algebraically constrain the Chern--Simons invariants of the complements S^3 \setminus 4_1, S^3 \setminus 5_2, and S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3. By the Chern--Simons/volume correspondence, this constraint would force holonomy contributions at different tower levels to close up after finitely many levels.

The cosimplicial structure theorem guarantees an infinite tower. The obstruction classes \kappa_n never simultaneously vanish. The crossed groupoid does not degenerate. This realizes the motivic perpetual obstruction theorem. The motivic Galois character of the substrate is non-trivial at every finite place p \nmid \chi(A). The class \kappa_n is the HKR image of that character at level n (Hochschild–Kummer connection). Consequently, \kappa_n cannot vanish at the corresponding cyclotomic levels. The algebraic independence of the volumes is the transcendence shadow of the non-vanishing motivic Galois character. The tower never terminates. No polynomial envelope binds the resulting volumes.

Rigorous proof requires controlling the arithmetic of the quantum dilogarithm at every tower level. This control demands new results analogous to Nesterenko's theorem on the algebraic independence of E-function values. These results must generalize to quantum dilogarithm series and the cosimplicial filtration of \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-gerbes.
rem:implications-algebraic-independence:
Remark Implications if the QOU volumes are algebraically independent. Assume the algebraic independence conjecture holds. No non-trivial polynomial P \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y, z] satisfies P(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) = 0.

Mathematical consequences.

  1. Milnor's conjecture. The knots 4_1, 5_2, and the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 have pairwise non-commensurable hyperbolic complements. Algebraic independence implies the \mathbb{Q}-linear independence predicted by Milnor.

  2. Irrationality. The volumes \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) are individually irrational.

  3. Bloch--Wigner transcendence. Each volume takes the form D(\xi) for an algebraic \xi in distinct number fields (\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}), the cubic field of 5_2, and \mathbb{Q}(i)). Independence yields provably transcendental values of the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm at algebraic arguments.

Framework consequences.

  1. Tower non-collapse. The bridge theorem equates independence with the non-vanishing of all obstruction classes \kappa_n \neq 0. The cosimplicial filtration of \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-gerbes is strictly infinite.

  2. Confinement. The hadronic binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} has no closed-form algebraic reduction. The infinite tower supplies the categorical signature of quark confinement.

  3. Specialisation. The evaluation map \iota \colon \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)] \to \mathbb{R} at q = q_0 is injective. The physical coefficient ring equals the formal Laurent polynomial ring.

  4. Bandwidth bounds. The information-bandwidth bounds \mathfrak{B}(q) are tight.

Requirement. Establishing independence requires an arithmetic theorem for the quantum dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q at algebraic arguments.
rem:implications-algebraic-dependence:
Remark Implications if the QOU volumes are algebraically dependent. Suppose the algebraic independence conjecture fails. A non-trivial polynomial P \in \mathbb{Q}[x, y, z] satisfies P(\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) = 0.

Mathematical consequences.

  1. Milnor's conjecture. Algebraic dependence is weaker than \mathbb{Q}-linear dependence. A dependence polynomial of degree greater than one does not refute Milnor's prediction of \mathbb{Q}-linear independence for pairwise non-commensurable hyperbolic 3-manifolds.

  2. Bloch--Wigner identities. Each volume takes the form D(\xi_K) for an algebraic \xi_K in distinct number fields. An algebraic dependence yields a \mathbb{Q}-polynomial identity among Bloch--Wigner values across \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}), the cubic field of 5_2, and \mathbb{Q}(i).

  3. Transcendence chain. The implication chain from independence to Borel--Zagier to single-volume irrationality breaks. Irrationality remains open for each volume. The categorical lever to prove it vanishes.

Framework consequences.

  1. Tower collapse. The contrapositive of the bridge theorem forces an obstruction class \kappa_n to vanish. The cosimplicial filtration terminates at finite depth.

  2. Confinement. The hadronic binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} reduces to a finite polynomial expression in q. Confinement does not require the infinite-tower structure.

  3. Borromean baryon. The distinction between the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 and a sum of Hopf pairs reduces to finite categorical data. The invariant identifying the proton as a three-body configuration is computable without the infinite tower.

  4. Coefficient ring. The evaluation map \iota is not injective. The physical ring \mathbb{Q}[q, q^{-1}][\mathrm{Vol}(4_1), \mathrm{Vol}(5_2), \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)] is smaller than the formal Laurent ring admits.

  5. Bandwidth bounds. The substrate satisfies the information-bandwidth bounds \mathfrak{B}(q) with slack. The topological mass formula, the Gröbner--Shirshov construction, and the spectral predictions remain valid. They reside in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] (see formal chain remark).

Consequence for the conditional results. Dependence implies that the independence hypothesis fails. The conditional implication from tower non-collapse to independence then holds only vacuously: its hypothesis, the Yekutieli lifting condition, is unsatisfiable.
conj:baryon-product-from-alt:
Conjecture The baryon integrand is the \mathrm{Alt}^3 Vandermonde of the color-sheet velocities. Let F(z, c) \in R[z, c] be the color-tube cubic (color-tube cubic) with roots c_1(z), c_2(z), c_3(z) over the categorical base ring R. Let \mathrm{S}_3 act on the three color sheets by permutation. The canonical Wedderburn decomposition is

  R[\mathrm{S}_3]
  \;\cong\;
  R \oplus R \oplus R^{2 \times 2}
  \quad
  (\text{trivial} \;\oplus\; \text{sign} \;\oplus\; \text{standard}).

Write v_k := dc_k/dz for the color-sheet velocities. The integrand

  \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}(z)
  \;:=\;
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} (v_j - v_i)
  \;=\;
  (v_2 - v_1)(v_3 - v_1)(v_3 - v_2)

is the Vandermonde in the velocities. It spans the lowest-degree part of the \mathrm{Alt}^3 (sign) isotype of R[v_1, v_2, v_3] under the \mathrm{S}_3 action permuting the sheets: every sign-isotypic polynomial is \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} times a symmetric one. The sum \sum_k v_k spans the degree-one part of the trivial isotype. The product \prod_k v_k is symmetric under sheet exchange and lies in the trivial isotype, not the sign isotype.

The integrand is R-rational up to the square root of the discriminant: \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} = r(z)\, V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3) with r \in R(z), and V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)^2 = \Delta(z) \in R[z]. This purely algebraic statement holds over R and does not use the archimedean fibre functor \tau \colon R \to \mathbb{R}.

The \mathrm{Alt}^3 isotype is a genuinely non-trivial sign line, not a channel indistinguishable from the trivial one. The monodromy of the color-tube cubic around its discriminant is the full \mathrm{S}_3 — computed exactly over R = \mathbb{Q}[z] and cross-checked at 50 digits (six simple branch points, each a transposition, together generating \mathrm{S}_3; monodromy witness) — so its sign character is surjective onto \{\pm 1\}. Fixing the baryon to this sign isotype therefore fixes the integrand up to a scalar.
rem:baryon-product-from-alt-proof-sketch:
Remark Proof sketch: baryon product from alt. Proof sketch. By Schur–Weyl duality at level n = 3 in three dimensions (Schur–Weyl mass decomposition), the \mathrm{S}_3-module

  V \;:=\; \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3}\, T_{c_k}\mathbf{C}
  \;\cong\; R\,\langle dc_1/dz,\ dc_2/dz,\ dc_3/dz\rangle

decomposes into isotypic components labelled by partitions of 3:

  V \;\cong\; V_{(3)} \;\oplus\; V_{(1,1,1)} \;\oplus\; V_{(2,1)}
  \;=\; \mathrm{Sym}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Alt}^3 \;\oplus\; \mathrm{Std}^{\oplus 2}.

The dimensions are \dim_R V_{(3)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(1,1,1)} = 1, \dim_R V_{(2,1)} = 2, summing to 4. However, since V is the rank-3 permutation representation of \mathrm{S}_3, V \cong V_{(3)} \oplus V_{(2,1)}. The rank-1 alternating piece sits inside the exterior cube \Lambda^3 V. The relevant isotype is therefore the top exterior power.

By the Frobenius character formula (Frobenius universal) applied to \mathrm{S}_3, the projector onto the sign isotype of any \mathrm{S}_3-module W is

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_3|} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\, \sigma
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6}\bigl(
    \mathrm{id} - (12) - (13) - (23) + (123) + (132)
  \bigr).

Applied to dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz \in V^{\otimes 3}, this projector yields the antisymmetrisation

  \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}}\bigl(dc_1/dz \otimes dc_2/dz \otimes dc_3/dz\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{6} \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{S}_3}
    \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\,
    \bigotimes_{k=1}^{3} dc_{\sigma(k)}/dz.

Write v_k := dc_k/dz. Under the canonical isomorphism \Lambda^3 V \cong R, the antisymmetrised tensor maps to v_1 \wedge v_2 \wedge v_3. On the diagonal frame \bigl(v_k\, e_k\bigr)_{k=1}^{3} this is \bigl(\prod_k v_k\bigr)\, e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3. The sign change under sheet exchange is carried by e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3, not by the coefficient: after the identification e_1 \wedge e_2 \wedge e_3 \mapsto 1, which is not \mathrm{S}_3-equivariant, the scalar \prod_k v_k is symmetric. So the product is not a sign-isotypic scalar.

The sign-isotypic scalars are the antisymmetric polynomials in v_1, v_2, v_3. Applying \pi_{\mathrm{Alt}} to the monomial v_1^0 v_2^1 v_3^2 gives \tfrac{1}{6}\sum_{\sigma} \mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)\, v_{\sigma(2)}\, v_{\sigma(3)}^2, which is \tfrac{1}{6} times the 3 \times 3 Vandermonde determinant. Its cofactor expansion factors as

  (v_2 v_3^2 - v_3 v_2^2) - v_1 (v_3^2 - v_2^2) + v_1^2 (v_3 - v_2)
  \;=\;
  (v_2 - v_1)(v_3 - v_1)(v_3 - v_2)
  \;=\; \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}},

an identity in any commutative ring. Every antisymmetric polynomial is divisible by each v_j - v_i, hence by \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}, with symmetric quotient; so \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} spans the lowest-degree part of the sign isotype.

R-rationality. By implicit differentiation v_k = -(\partial F/\partial z)/(\partial F/\partial c) at (z, c_k), a rational function of c_k over R(z). The ratio \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} / V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3) is symmetric in the roots, hence lies in R(z), and the squared Vandermonde of the roots is the discriminant of the cubic (color-tube cubic):

  V_3(c_1, c_2, c_3)^2
  \;=\;
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} (c_i - c_j)^2
  \;=\;
  \Delta(z)
  \;\in\; R[z].

So \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}}^2 \in R(z), and \lambda_{\mathrm{baryon}} itself lies in R(z)\bigl(\sqrt{\Delta(z)}\bigr). \square

The sum \sum_k dc_k/dz spans the degree-one part of the trivial isotype V_{(3)}, the integrand for a symmetric trion. Element of G Image of \varphi
(\mathrm{id}, \mathrm{id}) \varphi
(\tau, \mathrm{id}) -1/\varphi
(\mathrm{id}, \iota) 1/\varphi
(\tau, \iota) -\varphi
